Within weeks of completing high school, Ron Hatfield launched his pursuit of excellence by enlisting in the United States Marine Corps. During his five year tour as an active duty Marine, Ron served as an aviation electronics technician at various military bases all over the world, including more than six months in Saudi Arabia during Operation Desert Shield/Desert Storm. As an avionics tech, he was committed to troubleshooting and repairing a multitude of electronic equipment on his unit's aircraft in order to fulfill daily mission requirements, often making split-second decisions while maintaining utmost concern for quality and safety. He brings this same discipline, dedication, and intellectual skill to the practice of law at Jenkins Fenstermaker, PLLC.

Ron received his undergraduate degree (B.A. History) from Marshall University in 1997, and he is a 2000 graduate of the West Virginia University College of Law. As a practicing attorney, Ron has represented both business and individual clients in the diverse field of general civil litigation, concentrating on personal injury, property damage, construction defects, product liability, premises liability, motor vehicle accidents, and insurance coverage issues. Ron has been admitted to practice in the state courts of West Virginia, Kentucky, and North Carolina, as well as the United States District Courts in each of those states.

As an avionics tech, he was committed to troubleshooting and repairing a multitude of electronic equipment on his unit's aircraft in order to fulfill daily mission requirements, often making split-second decisions while maintaining utmost concern for quality and safety. He brings this same discipline, dedication, and intellectual skill to the practice of law at Jenkins Fenstermaker, PLLC.

Ron received his undergraduate degree (B.A. History) from Marshall University in 1997, and he is a 2000 graduate of the West Virginia University College of Law. As a practicing attorney, Ron has represented both business and individual clients in the diverse field of general civil litigation, concentrating on personal injury, property damage, construction defects, product liability, premises liability, motor vehicle accidents, and insurance coverage issues. Ron has been admitted to practice in the state courts of West Virginia, Kentucky, and North Carolina, as well as the United States District Courts in each of those states.

attorneys.name: R. Edison Hill
attorneys.firm_name: Hill, Peterson, Carper, Bee & Deitzler, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Charleston, WV
attorneys.bio:
R. Edison (Ed) Hill is senior member in the law firm of Hill, Peterson, Carper, Bee & Deitzler, PLLC. He founded this firm in June 1980. Mr. Hill is a trial attorney and spends his professional career exclusively representing individuals who have been seriously injured or families of those who have lost their lives as a result of others' negligence.

EDUCATION: R. Edison Hill began his education at West Virginia University where he obtained a B.A. degree in biology in 1972. He went on to attend West Virginia University College of Law and obtained his law degree in 1976.

PROFESSIONAL CAREER: Upon graduating from law school in 1976, Mr. Hill served as a law clerk to the Honorable K. K. Hall, Judge of the U. S. Circuit Court of Appeals, Fourth Circuit. Thereafter, he worked for a period of three years (1977-1980) as an associate for the law firm of Jackson, Kelly, Holt & O'Farrell in Charleston, West Virginia. In June 1980, Mr. Hill founded his own law firm in Charleston, West Virginia, which firm evolved to Hill & Peterson in 1984, and then to the present firm (Hill, Peterson, Carper, Bee & Deitzler, PLLC) in 1991.

PUBLIC SERVICE: R. Edison Hill currently serves as Chairman for the Central West Virginia Regional Airport Authority, which is the governing board for the West Virginia International Yeager Airport, located in Charleston, West Virginia. He has served on the Yeager Airport Board of Directors since July 1993.

PROFESSIONAL ORGANIZATIONS: Mr. Hill is a member of the following: American Association for Justice (Life Member); The National Trial Lawyers: Top 100; West Virginia Association for Justice (Served as President 1993-94); West Virginia State Bar; Kanawha County Bar Association; Lawyer-Pilots Bar Association; Consumer Attorneys of West Virginia; Mr. Hill was selected into the RoundTable: America's 100 Most Influential Trial Lawyers, by the Trial Lawyer magazine.

AWARDS: Awarded 2005 "Trial Lawyer of the Year" by Trial Lawyers for Public Justice for successful class action litigation in West Virginia in the case of Leach, et al. v E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company, Circuit Court of Wood County, West Virginia, Civil Action No. 01-C-608, which case involved drinking water contaminated by the chemical ammonium perfluorooctanoate acid ("PFOA" or "C-8"), a chemical utilized in the manufacture of Teflon. DuPont paid $105 million to settle phase one of this litigation, with potential payout of an additional $235 million for medical monitoring. Multi-district litigation in federal court regarding diseases to individuals caused by this chemical resulted in settlements in excess of $700 million.

"Fellow" of the West Virginia Bar Foundation. Awarded 2008.

Recipient of the "Clarence Darrow Award" in 2014. The Darrow Award is given to attorneys who have demonstrated conviction in their work and exceptional courage in the face of adversity. This award is given out every year during the Mass Torts Made Possible Conference in Las Vegas by national trial attorney and radio talk show host Mike Papantonio.

PERSONAL INTERESTS: Mr. Hill is an aviation enthusiast and has held a private pilot's license since 1984. He is instrument rated and qualified to fly multi-engine aircraft. He currently operates a Beechcraft Baron and utilizes this aircraft for personal and professional traveling. As a lover of exotic plants, Mr. Hill enjoys growing a variety of orchids in his greenhouse.

Mr. Hill's biographical information above includes reference to specific and cumulative case results of the past and should not be misconstrued as any indication that a future client or case will have a similar outcome. Case results depend on a variety of factors unique to each case. Past case results do not guarantee or predict a similar result in any future case undertaken by R. Edison Hill or this law firm.

attorneys.practice_type: Workplace Injury Lawyers in Charleston, WV
attorneys.bio:
Lee Javins was spent the last 20+ years primarily representing injured workers and their survivors. Most cases involve some combination of workplace liability and product liability involving heavy equipment accidents, logging, electrical injuries and coal mining. Occasionally, Mr. Javins is retained to represent the State in issues ranging from WVU’s departure from the Big East Conference to enforcement actions on behalf of the Attorney General.

Workplace Safety

Recovery on behalf of a timber cutter who suffered a traumatic amputation of his leg due to unsafe logging practices

Recovery on behalf of a widow whose husband was killed in a roof collapse in an underground mine

Recovery on behalf of a widow whose husband was killed when an unsecured log fell from a log truck during the unloading process

Recovery on behalf of a widow whose husband was electrocuted while working on an unsafe power center in an underground coal mine

Recovery on behalf of a coal miner who was crushed by mine cable which had been caught in the cutter head of a continuous miner

Verdict for a teenager whose hand was crushed by a hydraulic log splitter

Recovery on behalf of a coal miner who sustained severe head trauma following a collision with a locomotive in an underground mine

Recovery on behalf of the family of a project engineer who was fatally injured when an end loader with a disabled warning buzzer backed over him

Recovery on behalf of a coal miner who was severely injured following the collapse of a large stacker belt

Recovery on behalf of a coal miner whose head was pinned against the mine roof following an unexpected activation of a continuous miner

Recovery on behalf of a timber cutter who suffered degloving injuries to both legs after a run away log rolled over him

Recovery on behalf of a coal miner who suffered a crushed foot due to a poorly maintained longwall shield

Recovery on behalf of a coal miner who was paralyzed following the fall of an improperly supported mine rib

Recovery on behalf of a timber cutter who was paralyzed by a falling tree limb as a result of unsafe cutting practices

Recovery on behalf of a coal miner who sustained severe electrical injuries caused by poorly insulated mining cable

Recovery on behalf of a coal miner who was paralyzed as a result of an unsupported mine rib

Recovery on behalf of an electrical worker who fell from a raised work position following an electrical shock from an improperly grounded electrical component

Verdict for a rock truck driver who fell from his truck due to an unsafe access ladder

Recovery on behalf of a widow whose husband was fatally injured while operating an excavator beyond its capability as required by his employer

Recovery on behalf of a cable worker who was impaled by a corrugated metal fence post following an electrical shock while on a utility pole

Recovery on behalf of a construction worker whose leg injuries required over 20 surgeries as a result of a fall from an improperly guarded construction site

Recovery on behalf of a coal miner who sustained degloving injuries to his arm as a result of a poorly maintained shuttle car

Recovery on behalf of a widower whose wife sustained fatal injuries whose automobile rolled over a steep parking lot embankment as a result of inadequate guard rails

Recovery on behalf of a part-time construction helper who sustained severe head trauma following a 20 foot fall through an unguarded hole in the construction site roof

Recovery on behalf of three injured employees who sustained injuries including paralysis as a result of a building collapse

Recovery on behalf of an HVAC worker who fell from an extension ladder, shattering both feet, while servicing rooftop equipment due to no permanent fixed access being offered.

Recovery on behalf of a mine worker who sustained permanent hand injuries due to improper training and securement on a vulcanizing unit.

Product Liability

Recovery on behalf of a woman who suffered paralysis to her arm following an ATV accident caused by a defective gear shifter

Recovery on behalf of a coal miner who suffered severe neck injuries due to the defective design of a coal hauler operator compartment

Recovery on behalf of a hunter who suffered paralysis to his leg following the collapse of a climbing tree stand

Recovery on behalf of a widow whose husband was fatally injured when his lawn tractor lost control due to a defective transmission

Recovery on behalf of a widow whose husband was fatally injured while changing a tire on a defective multi-piece truck rim

Recovery on behalf of a passenger of a vehicle which overturned, causing the roof to collapse. During the rollover, the passenger's occupant protection system failed to adequately secure the plaintiff's body causing severe and debilitating spinal cord injuries rendering him a partial quadriplegic.

Other

Recovery on behalf of a widower whose wife was killed when a roadside tree fell onto her automobile

Recovery on behalf of a young man who was paralyzed in an ATV collision as a result of inadequate training

Represented West Virginia University in its litigation concerning its departure from the Big East Conference

Recovery on behalf of a mother and daughter who sustained debilitating neck and back injuries when a roadside tree fell onto their vehicle.

attorneys.name: Meridith O. Johnstone
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Charleston, WV
attorneys.bio:
With a background that includes representation of Social Security Disability claimants and plaintiffs in personal injury cases, Social Security Attorney/Claimant Representative Meredith Johnstone brings a unique perspective to her role with the Jan Dils team.

After receiving her B.A. with honors from the University of Kentucky, Lexington, Meredith went on to graduate from the West Virginia University College of Law.

She then participated in the Clinical Law Program where she began learning about the rewards of assisting claimants in Social Security Disability claims, and successfully represented her first claimant.

After working with two law firms, in 2013 Meredith joined the West Virginia Ethics Commission, a state agency, as Deputy General Counsel, serving in that capacity until she joined Jan Dils, Attorneys at Law.

"As an attorney, I have met many hard-working people whose lives have been changed by illness, injury, and unexpected circumstances so that they can no longer work," said Meredith. "I imagine the help that I would want to receive in that situation, and offer that help to my clients."

At her best when she is talking with clients about their cases and putting their minds at ease about what to expect from the claim process, Meredith works to capture all the important facts so that each client's case can be presented well, and they feel that their personal story has been told.

When she's not busy getting to know each client and learning about their life experiences, Meredith enjoys vacationing at the beach, watching movies, working in the garden, and spending time with her husband, daughter, and their two cats at home.

We think you'll agree that Meredith is an excellent addition to our team-please join us in welcoming her to the Jan Dils family!

attorneys.name: Jeffrey T. Jones
attorneys.practice_type: Plaintiffs: Personal Injury Lawyers in Charleston, WV
attorneys.bio:
A native of Clarksburg, WV, Jeff received his undergraduate degree from Lenoir-Rhyne University in Hickory N.C. and his law degree from the West Virginia University College of Law. He began practicing law in Charleston in 1986 with the nationally known law firm of Preiser and Wilson, which later became Hunt and Wilson. Prior to joining Farmer, Cline and Campbell, Jeff was in solo practice for 16 years.

Jeff is the Past President of the West Virginia Association for Justice and was named Member of the Year in 1999. He is also the former editor of the Association’s magazine “The Advocate”. He is also the past President of the Lenoir-Rhyne Alumni Association and was the recipient of the Moretz Alumni Award for Service to the Alumni Association in 2006.

Jeff has been named one of the Top 100 Trial lawyers in West Virginia by The American Trial Lawyers Association and has been ranked as one of the Top 10 Personal Injury Attorneys in West Virginia by the National Academy of Personal Injury Attorneys. He is also a member of the Million Dollar Advocates Forum, recognizing those lawyers who have either a million dollar verdict or settlement. He was named an Emerging Business Leader to watch in USA Today in 2012.

He is the author of the best-selling book “Protect and Defend” and also authored “The West Virginia Automobile Accident and Injury Guide”. He has also appeared as a contributor on the national internet radio show Money for Lunch to discuss issues related to injury victims and insurance companies.

Jeff’s practice is concentrated in the areas of helping victims injured in car accidents, wrongful death victims and their families and other personal injury victims. He also does trial work.

attorneys.name: Ashley L. Justice
attorneys.firm_name: Pullin, Fowler, Flanagan, Brown & Poe, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Appellate Advocacy Lawyers in Beckley, WV
attorneys.bio:
Ashley Justice graduated Summa Cum Laude from Marshall University in 2003, with a Bachelor of Arts Degree in International Affairs and minors in Spanish and Political Science. While attending Marshall University, Ashley earned the Highest Honors in International Affairs award, became certified to teach English as a foreign language, and studied abroad in Madrid, Spain. She graduated from the West Virginia University College of Law in May, 2006 and received the Order of the Barristers award.

Ashley began working as a law clerk in Pullin, Fowler, Flanagan, Brown & Poe, PLLC's Morgantown, West Virginia office during her first year of law school. Upon graduation, she relocated to the Charleston branch of Pullin, Fowler, Flanagan, Brown & Poe, PLLC, where she practiced asbestos, toxic tort and general insurance defense litigation. In October 2007, Ashley returned to her hometown to work in the firm's Beckley, West Virginia office. She is admitted to practice before the West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals, the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of West Virginia, the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the U.S. District Court for the Northern Division of West Virginia.

Ashley Justice was born in Beckley, West Virginia on December 6, 1980. She resided in Port St. Lucie, Florida for five years before returning to Beckley. Ashley enjoys spending time with family, friends, her four dogs - Hunter Brown, Sherman, Max and Maggie, and her cat, Buddy. Her hobbies include rescuing animals, traveling, Shotokan Karate, reading, and motorcycling.

attorneys.name: Nathanial A. Kuratomi
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Lawyers in Huntington, WV
attorneys.bio:
Nathanial Kuratomi's practice is devoted entirely to litigation, with emphases on police and municipal liability, employment law, deliberate intent, Workers' Compensation and workplace injury law, and premises liability. Mr. Kuratomi defends police officers and municipalities in state and federal civil rights cases. He also represents companies in both civil and administrative proceedings related to various employment-related claims, such as harassment, retaliation, and discrimination, and represents employers in "deliberate intent" actions for excess damages related to alleged workplace injuries and in litigated Workers' Compensation matters.

Mr. Kuratomi received his B.A. in Literature and B.A. in Creative Writing from Marshall University in 2002 and his J.D. from the Dickinson School of Law of the Pennsylvania State University in 2006 with a Certificate in Alternative Dispute Resolution and Advocacy. He was the Paul L. Stevens Memorial Scholarship recipient, was granted the ABA/BNA Award for Excellence in the Study of Labor and Employment Law, was a member of the Appellate Moot Court Board, and served as the Managing Editor of the Journal of American Arbitration.

Mr. Kuratomi is admitted to practice in West Virginia, the United States Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals, and the United States District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of West Virginia. Mr. Kuratomi is a member of the American Bar Association, the West Virginia Bar Association, the Defense Trial Counsel of West Virginia, and the Defense Research Institute.

attorneys.name: Marvin W. Masters
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Charleston, WV
attorneys.bio:
Marvin W. Masters was born and raised in Greenbrier, West Virginia. Mr. Masters received his Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering from West Virginia University in 1967 and his law degree from West Virginia University in 1972. He founded The Masters Law Firm, l.c. in 1974 to fight for the injured and to provide a voice for fair and just compensation.

He is experienced in litigating serious personal injury, car accidents, trucking accidents, medical malpractice, wrongful death, and property damage cases, as well as product liability cases, including drug litigation. With over 50 years of experience practicing as a trial attorney, Mr. Masters is licensed and has presented cases in front of the West Virginia Supreme Court and all lower courts as well as the United States Supreme Court.

Mr. Masters is well known and respected in the legal and local communities. He has built a reputation for tackling both big corporations and negligent individuals with the same level of legal vigor and fortitude. His skillful legal practice garnered national attention when Mr. Masters acquired a $ 404 million settlement verdict in a gas royalties’ case, one of the largest settlements in the state of West Virginia. His multi-million-dollar successes awarded him entry into the Million Dollar Advocates Forum, one of the most prestigious groups of trial lawyers in the country. Membership is limited to attorneys who have won million and multi-million-dollar verdicts and settlements. Fewer than 1% of U.S. lawyers hold this distinction.

In addition, Mr. Masters has been awarded the honor of “Best Lawyers in America” for a consecutive 20 years, has been recognized by Best Lawyers since 2001, Super Lawyers, “Top Litigator” Award, was included in the “Top 100 Trial Lawyer” list by the National Trial Lawyers and was named “2024 Attorney of the Year” by “Top 100 Lawyers”.

The Masters Law Firm, l.c., has received the Martindale-Hubbell Preeminent recognition for the Highest Level of Professional Excellence.

Mr. Masters is a member of the West Virginia State Bar, American Bar Association, American Association for Justice, and The American College of Trial Lawyers. He previously held the title of President for the West Virginia Association for Justice,

Decades of litigating experience have allowed Mr. Masters to settle multi-million-dollar settlements and verdicts. His notable claims have prompted mentions in Esquire, West Virginia Record, WV Gazette and the State Journal.

attorneys.name: Jeremy M. McGraw
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Moundsville, WV
attorneys.bio:
Jeremy McGraw is a personal injury and nursing home abuse lawyer at Gold Khourey & Turak. Jeremy has represented seriously injured and damaged individuals in many different areas of the law.

When a person suffers an injury due to the careless actions of another or at the hands of corporate greed, Jeremy knows what it takes to get justice for his clients. While justice can be measured in different ways, Jeremy understands that in many situations the law measures justice by the type of results he obtains in his cases. Jeremy’s focus is always first and foremost on getting those results. With multiple million-dollar settlements to his name, people can count on Jeremy to obtain the results they deserve when the stakes are highest.

While Jeremy handles all types of personal injury cases—from car accidents to workplace, industrial and oil and gas injuries—Jeremy’s passion is his focus on nursing home abuse and neglect cases. Jeremy understands that the decision to place a loved one with a nursing home or other care facility is never an easy one to make. Nursing homes serve a very important role in our society. Many families simply don’t have the ability or resources to care for those that need around the clock care. Those families trust nursing homes to provide their loved one with not only exceptional care but to treat them with dignity and respect. When that trust is violated and a loved one is injured, Jeremy knows that the damage can be far-reaching.

In addition to his extensive personal injury practice, Jeremy has the knowledge and experience to handle a variety of nursing home abuse and neglect cases involving the following injuries and more:

Bed sores

Falls

Medication errors

Malnutrition / Dehydration

Dehydration

Mental, psychological, or sexual abuse

Financial abuse

Brian D. Morrison is a Member at Bailey & Wyant, PLLC's Charleston office. He is admitted to practice in the State of West Virginia, the United States District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of West Virginia, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit. He is a member of the West Virginia Bar Association, the Kanawha County Bar Association, the Defense Trial Counsel of West Virginia, and the Defense Research Institute. After obtaining his Bachelor of Arts degree in Criminal Justice from Marshall University, Brian attended the West Virginia University College of Law, from where he graduated in 1997. While at law school, Brian participated in the Clinical Law program, gaining invaluable experience representing clients across the state.

Brian concentrates his practice on civil litigation, including personal injury litigation, premises liability, contractual disputes, insurance coverage disputes and insurance bad faith litigation. His practice encompasses 55 counties, and in some cases, neighboring states. He has had numerous trials throughout the state and has argued key cases before the West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals.

In his spare time, he enjoys golfing, scuba diving, hiking, mountain biking and spending time with his family.

attorneys.name: Matthew H. Nelson
attorneys.practice_type: Labor Law Lawyers in Morgantown, WV
attorneys.bio:
Matt Nelson has spent most of his life in Morgantown, West Virginia. After graduating from West Virginia University, Matt attended The Ohio State University Moritz College of Law, where he received the Dean's Award for Excellence and was a member of the Appellate Advocacy Advisory Committee. Since then, Matt has developed a state and region wide litigation practice with two of West Virginia's largest law firms, and has been recognized as a "Rising Star" by Super Lawyers. Matt joined Farmer, Cline & Campbell in 2012, focusing his practice on labor and employment law, as well as general litigation, personal injury litigation and construction law.

Over the years, Matt has represented both corporations and individuals in complex employment issues and personal injury claims. He has advised clients on the intricacies of both federal and state employment and commercial laws. Matt has also handled several administrative cases before various federal and state agencies and is one of only a few attorneys to have argued before the Federal Mine Safety and Health Review Commission within the past few years.

Matt is heavily involved in the local community and currently serves on the Board of Directors for Senior Monongalians, Inc.

attorneys.name: Stephen P. New
attorneys.firm_name: Stephen P. New, Attorney at Law
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Beckley, WV
attorneys.bio:
Stephen New is a native of Gilbert, West Virginia, living and practicing law in Beckley. He is a 1990 graduate of Gilbert High School and 1994 graduate of Marshall University, B.A. Political Science.

Stephen is a 1998 graduate of the West Virginia University College of Law, Order of the Barristers. While a student at the College of Law, Stephen was the Chief justice of the Moot Court Board and a member of the Lugar Trial Association. Stephen participated in WVU’s Baker Cup Tournament and represented WVU at Vanderbilt University’s first amendment Moot Court Tournament in March 1998. Stephen was the top ranked Lugar trial advocate and represented WVU in the ATLA National Trial Advocacy Tournament. Stephen was one of the first 10 Judicial Law Clerks employed by the West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals and clerked for the Raleigh County Circuit Judges. In August 1999, Stephen joined Pamela A. Lambert’s law practice in Gilbert until leaving to start his own office in May 2004.

Stephen concentrates his practice primarily in personal injury, wrongful death and employment discrimination. He has tried 44 cases to jury verdict primarily motor vehicle accidents, medical malpractice, employment discrimination and environmental/toxic tort. Stephen has made seven appearances before the West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals. Stephen is licensed in all courts in West Virginia. He is licensed before the United States District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of West Virginia, and the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals. He is a member of the American Association of Justice and the West Virginia Association of Justice, serving as a member of the Executive Committee and on its Board of Directors. Stephen is President-Elect of the West Virginia Association for Justice, and is slated to become President June 1, 2018. He has spoken in West Virginia on the topics of coal mining safety regulations, workers compensation law, and military law/USERRA.

The Law Office of Stephen New has represented individuals in a wide array of cases including prominent class actions, resulting in large sums of monetary compensation and peace of mind from holding responsible those who cause harm. Stephen was co lead counsel for the nursing students in the Mountain State University litigation. Stephen has been and is currently litigating mass environmental damage cases. Most recently, Stephen and Mandy are currently co lead counsel for the unfortunate patients of the Raleigh Heart Clinic. The cardiologist running the heart clinic caused approximately 150 to contract hepatitis B and C. Stephen will long be remembered for his victory at the West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals on behalf of his client Diana Dickerson who illegally had her widows benefits taken away by a workers compensation insurance carrier and later lost her home. Stephen took the case to the Supreme Court and was able to have Ms. Dickerson and other widows’ benefits restored to them.

Stephen retired as a Major with the West Virginia Army National Guard in May 2009. Stephen enlisted December 23, 1988. He completed Army ROTC at Marshall and was commissioned as an Armor officer. He has served at Ft. Knox, KY, Ft. Bliss, TX, Ft. Bragg, NC, Ft. Dix, NJ and elsewhere. Stephen retired as the Deputy Commander of Camp Dawson in Kingwood, West Virginia.

Stephen is married to his wife of 19 years, Amy and they have one daughter, Rebekah, who is 13. They enjoy concerts, boating, Marshall University sports, and are actively involved in Theatre West Virginia where Stephen serves as President of the Board. Stephen and his family are members of Faith Community Church and are actively involved with the youth. Of the many things Stephen and Amy are proud of, their firms’ philanthropy is at the top of the list. Since 2004, and resulting from one of Stephen’s real-life interactions with a client, Stephen and Amy have given away over 12,000 bicycle helmets to children and safety groups throughout West Virginia.

attorneys.name: Robert Noone
attorneys.practice_type: Workers Compensation Lawyers in Charleston, WV
attorneys.bio:
Robert Noone has represented injured workers from "day one" in a legal career that began over 25 years ago. A past partner in the labor law firm of Crandall & Pyles, he formed Robert Noone Legal Services (1989) in Logan, WV, continuing his primarily focus on workers compensation and social security. He has served as a past chairperson of the State Bar Workers Compensation Committee and lectured for bar and professional associations on topics of workers compensation, occupational pneumoconiosis and law office management. In the mid-90's he helped create Logan Health Right to provide free health care to the area's uninsured.

Noone also enjoys a concentration in juvenile law which resulted in the WV Supreme Court of Appeals first placing him on the Juvenile Justice Committee (1992) and later on the Court Improvement Project which has sought to improve delivery of services to abused and neglected children in the court system. He is a founding member and current Chairperson of the Logan County Child Advocacy Center, started in 2008.

Since 2003, Robert Noone has worked in close association with Bailey, Javins & Carter, L.C., serving in the capacity "of counsel" to them in the Logan community, as they offer comprehensive legal representation and advocacy.

On the not-so-serious side, Noone is known nationally as an entertainer in the legal world touring with "The Bob Noone Show" (a/k/a "Bob Noone and The Well Hung Jury"). Having several CDs and a DVD to his credit, his audiences range from Federal Supreme Court Justices to family physicians in venues stretching from Hawaii to the Greenbrier Resort. More info at www.lawsongs.com

attorneys.name: Charlotte Ann Hoffman Norris
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Huntington, WV
attorneys.bio:
Charlotte has over 26 years of experience practicing employment law, healthcare law, professional licensure and malpractice, commercial law, insurance coverage, and product liability law. She recently expanded her areas of practice to include special education law, as a natural extension of her employment law practice and issues of disability accommodation. Charlotte also has represented financial industry clients before FINRA. Her experience includes serving for 2 years as in-house general counsel to a hospital client. Throughout her career, Charlotte's professional focus has been to provide her clients with the tools necessary to obtain the best results whether the issues involved personnel management, negotiated transaction or adversarial proceedings.

Charlotte graduated from Agnes Scott College and Washington and Lee University School of Law. As an undergraduate, she was inducted into Phi Beta Kappa and the Mortar Board Society, and graduated with High Honors. As a law student, she was appointed to serve as Co-Director of the Western State Hospital Legal Aid Society.

In 2016, Charlotte was recognized by Chambers U.S.A. for Employment Litigation. She also has been recognized by The Best Lawyers in America under the categories of Employment Law Management, ERISA Litigation and Healthcare Law. Best Lawyers honored Charlotte in 2016 as one of its Women Lawyers of the Year (West Virginia).

Charlotte is admitted to practice in all of the courts of West Virginia and Kentucky, as well as the United States District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of West Virginia and the United States Courts of Appeal for the Fourth and Sixth Circuits. She is a Member of the West Virginia Bar Association, the Cabell County (WV) Bar Association, the Kentucky Bar Association, the American Bar Association, the Defense Research Institute, the Defense Trial Counsel of West Virginia ("DTCWV"), and the Council of Parent Attorneys and Advocates. Charlotte is a past Chair of the Employment Law Committee for DTCWV.

Charlotte has lectured to professional groups in multiple areas of employment law, as well as on issues involving managing troubled professionals, medical malpractice defense, physician-patient communications, health information management, mental health law, psychiatric forensics, and elder and child abuse law. She has also published articles on psychiatric malpractice, medical monitoring, the Privacy Standards under HIPAA, and EMTALA.

In addition to her professional activities, Charlotte is a Member of the 2016 Class for Leadership West Virginia and currently serves on the Boards of the Facing Hunger Food Bank and Prestera Center for Mental Health Services, Inc. She lives in Huntington with her husband and son.

Throughout his legal career, Jon has developed an extensive trial and appellate practice in the areas of Product Liability, Toxic Tort, Construction Law, Medical Malpractice, Automobile and Trucking Litigation, Medical Device and Drug Litigation, Employment Law, and general Insurance Defense. He serves as national coordinating counsel for a corporate client defending tens of thousands of asbestos lawsuits across the country. Jon also represents product manufacturers, premises owners, and employers in toxic tort litigation.

Jon is a graduate of Washington & Lee University and the West Virginia University College of Law. He is admitted to practice in West Virginia (1998) and Kentucky (1999), as well as before the United States Supreme Court, the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit, and the United States District Court for the Southern District of West Virginia. He is an Active member of the Defense Trial Counsel of West Virginia, DRI, and IADC.

attorneys.name: David Pence
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Charleston, WV
attorneys.bio:
David Pence is a native of South Charleston, West Virginia and a graduate from the West Virginia University College of Law. Mr. Pence has developed a reputation for excellence in defending individuals accused of driving under the influence (DUI) throughout West Virginia. His reputation for winning is a result of his success in defending drivers before juries and administrative hearing examiners throughout West Virginia.

As a member of the National College of DUI Defense, Mr. Pence frequently attends seminars throughout the country to stay attuned to new tactics to better defend his clients. He is a certified operator of the Intoximeter EC/IR II breath machine used by law enforcement in West Virginia. Mr. Pence also received certified training in defending drivers accused of being impaired by controlled substances. As Mr. Pence says, "The key to winning is knowing more about the law, the science and the facts than your adversary. Always be prepared."

Mr. Pence also represents disabled works fighting to obtain their Social Security Disability Benefits. As a sustaining member of the National Organization of Social Security Claimants’ Representative (NOSSCR), Mr. Pence has a vast knowledge of the Social Security claims process and welcomes the opportunity to put his skills to work for you!

Recently, Mr. Pence was voted as a Top Lawyer of West Virginia by Super Lawyer’s Magazine for excellence and achievements in the legal community. As an advocate, Mr. Pence has the required combination of skill, knowledge and compassion necessary to help achieve the desired result.

In addition to his legal work, Mr. Pence also enjoys coaching youth basketball at his local church and spending time with his family.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Charleston, WV
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Peterson’s biographical information below includes reference to specific and cumulative case results of the past and should not be misconstrued as any indication that a future client or case will have a similar outcome. Case results depend on a variety of factors unique to each case. Past case results do not guarantee or predict a similar result in any future case undertaken by James Peterson or this law firm.

James C. Peterson graduated from William Mitchell College of Law in Minnesota in 1976. Since graduation, he has been involved in a variety of legal pursuits, including acting as a law clerk for a Minnesota state trial court judge, serving as chief corporate counsel for a worldwide non-profit organization, and for the past thirty four years, concentrating his efforts in litigating severe personal injury, medical and legal malpractice and insurance bad faith cases, as well as mass tort/class action litigation involving defective products, pharmaceuticals, and insurance products. He is currently Of Counsel with the law firm of Hill, Peterson, Carper, Bee & Deitzler, P.L.L.C. since 1983.

Representative cases settled and/or tried to jury verdict include multi-million dollar medical and legal malpractice cases, recoveries in excess of $1 million in product liability cases, numerous million dollar verdicts and/or settlements involving serious motor vehicle accidents, as well as serving as co-lead counsel on the settlement of the largest pharmaceutical class action litigation in the history of the state of West Virginia, involving the diet drug fen-phen.

The firm is in the forefront of handling nuisance lawsuits filed on behalf of hundreds of individuals in West Virginia who have been affected and impacted by the Marcellus Shale drilling boom.

Mr. Peterson has been board-certified as a civil trial specialist by the National Board of Trial Advocacy (NBTA) since 1990. He has served in a variety of positions with both state and national trial lawyer organizations, including president of the West Virginia Trial Lawyers' Association (1996-1997). He is presently certified to practice in the states of Minnesota, Ohio, and West Virginia, and has been admitted pro hac vice in over a dozen other jurisdictions. While serving as chief corporate counsel for an international non-profit organization in the late 1970's, Mr. Peterson argued cases before several foreign jurisdictions.

Since 1987, Mr. Peterson has presented over 40 papers and articles nationwide on various legal topics in over two dozen states. Other legal publications include a chapter in a book published by the National Brain Injury Association involving hedonic damages; an article on the same topic appearing in the monthly publication Trial for the Association of Trial Lawyers of America (American Association for Justice), and a law review article entitled "Trial Techniques – Selecting and Using Expert Witnesses in Bad Faith Cases," 19 Am. Jour. Trial Adv., 543, (Spring 1996), Cumberland School of Law, Samford University, Birmingham, Alabama.

Mr. Peterson is recognized as a life member of American Association for Justice. He has been Board Certified as a Civil Trial Specialist by the National Board of Trial Advocacy (NBTA) since 1990 and in 2008, he, along with two of his Partners was awarded the "Trial Lawyer of the Year" by Trial Lawyers for Public Justice for successful class action litigation in the case of Leach et al vs. E.I. DuPont de Nemours and Company.

attorneys.name: Harvey D. Peyton
attorneys.practice_type: Courtroom Litigation Lawyers in Nitro, WV
attorneys.bio:
Born in 1949 to the late Tom H. Peyton and Anne T. Peyton, Mr. Peyton is a lifelong resident of West Virginia

A native of St. Albans, West Virginia, Harvey D. Peyton was admitted to practice law in the State of West Virginia immediately upon graduation from the West Virginia University College of Law in 1974. After a one-year clerkship with Chief Judge Robert E. Maxwell of the United States District Court for the Northern District of West Virginia, Mr. Peyton began practicing in the law office of Andrew J. Goodwin with a concentration on insurance defense trial work. In 1977, Mr. Peyton began practicing in Nitro, West Virginia, representing a wide range of civil litigants. Currently, he concentrates his practice on plaintiffs’ civil and criminal defense trial work in the Circuit Courts of Kanawha, Putnam and Mason Counties of West Virginia, and in local federal district courts. He is a member of the Putnam County Bar Association, the West Virginia State Bar, the West Virginia Bar Association, the West Virginia Association for Justice and the American Association for Justice. He is a past president of the West Virginia Association for Justice (formerly the West Virginia Trial Lawyers Association) and the West Virginia Bar Association. During a career that has now spanned almost 50 years of active practice, Mr. Peyton has completed well over two hundred jury trials involving wrongful death, serious personal injury, business disputes, claims under the Federal Employers Liability Act and criminal matters ranging from burglary and robbery to first degree murder.

Mr. Peyton believes that one’s highest goal is to help others who may be less fortunate. With his latest gifts to WVU and other institutions, the value of Mr. Peyton’s charitable gifts has exceeded a million and a half dollars.

Mr. Peyton is married to the former Jennifer Bailey of Poca, West Virginia, a graduate of Marshall University. He is the father of three children, Tom, Sarah and George, two of whom studied at WVU and all three of whom graduated from Marshall University.

attorneys.name: Edgar Allen Poe Jr.
attorneys.firm_name: Pullin, Fowler, Flanagan, Brown & Poe, PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Construction Law Lawyers in Charleston, WV
attorneys.bio:
Edgar Allen Poe, Jr. was born on September 25, 1952 in Wheeling, West Virginia. He grew up in Wheeling, Ohio County, West Virginia and graduated from Triadelphia High School. Growing up in Wheeling, West Virginia (a small but cosmopolitan family-oriented community) allowed Mr. Poe access to perform with the Oglebay Institute Towngate Theater in which he acted, directed and provided technical support for numerous productions in his high school and college years. Wheeling also had an active Youth Bowling Program. Mr. Poe participated in, and, with his team, won the Youth Bowling Championship for the state of West Virginia two years in a row. Mr. Poe's father was District Manager of the Social Security Office in Wheeling and also an instructor at Belmont Technical College. Mr. Poe's mother was a life-long teacher of World History at Triadelphia High School. This strong family emphasis on education helped Mr. Poe excel academically during his high school years. He graduated from Triadelphia High School as one of the top graduates in his class. The Wheeling area also afforded him an opportunity to become an avid skier.

Mr. Poe left the Wheeling, West Virginia area to pursue his undergraduate degree at the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, Virginia. During his tenure at the University of Virginia, he continued his academic pursuits, graduating with distinction. He continued his passion for theater and skiing and began the study of the martial art known as Tae Kwon Do.

Mr. Poe's interest in religion, literature and philosophy led him to seek his Master of Arts degree from the Divinity School of the University of Chicago with an emphasis in religion and literature. He graduated from the University of Chicago in 1977.

Mr. Poe returned to his home state of West Virginia to attend law school at the West Virginia University College of Law and graduated in 1980. Mr. Poe distinguished himself academically at the West Virginia University College of Law serving as a member of The Law Review, The Moot Court Board, The Order of the Barristers and as Chairman of The International Moot Court Team. After law school, Mr. Poe spent one year as a writ clerk at the West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals and one year as the personal clerk to Justice Thomas B. Miller of the West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals before going into private practice.

Mr. Poe began his career at The Law Offices of David L. Shuman and eventually formed the firm of Shuman, Annand and Poe in 1984. This firm, devoted to Insurance Defense Litigation, grew rapidly over the years and expanded from Charleston to Wheeling. Mr. Poe, having practiced with J. Victor Flanagan, joined Pullin, Fowler & Flanagan in 1999. During the entire course of his professional career he has devoted his work to insurance defense litigation and to the quality and cost-effective representation of insurance companies and their insureds.

Mr. Poe continues to be involved in these various activities, continues to practice the martial art of Tae Kwon Do at the S.H. Kang Tae Kwon Do Academy in South Charleston, West Virginia. He serves as legal counsel and is a member of the USTW (United States Tae Kwon Do Won). His son, Adam, is presently an undergraduate at George Washington University in Washington, D.C. His son, Sam, is presently a high school student and resides in Hilton Head, South Carolina where he enjoys fishing. Mr. Poe's daughter, Moraine, graduated from the University of California in Santa Cruz and is pursing her PhD as a Nurse Practitioner at Western University in California.

Mr. Poe's mother was a life-long teacher of World History at Triadelphia High School. This strong family emphasis on education helped Mr. Poe excel academically during his high school years. He graduated from Triadelphia High School as one of the top graduates in his class. The Wheeling area also afforded him an opportunity to become an avid skier.

Mr. Poe left the Wheeling, West Virginia area to pursue his undergraduate degree at the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, Virginia. During his tenure at the University of Virginia, he continued his academic pursuits, graduating with distinction. He continued his passion for theater and skiing and began the study of the martial art known as Tae Kwon Do.

Mr. Poe's interest in religion, literature and philosophy led him to seek his Master of Arts degree from the Divinity School of the University of Chicago with an emphasis in religion and literature. He graduated from the University of Chicago in 1977.

Mr. Poe returned to his home state of West Virginia to attend law school at the West Virginia University College of Law and graduated in 1980. Mr. Poe distinguished himself academically at the West Virginia University College of Law serving as a member of The Law Review, The Moot Court Board, The Order of the Barristers and as Chairman of The International Moot Court Team. After law school, Mr. Poe spent one year as a writ clerk at the West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals and one year as the personal clerk to Justice Thomas B. Miller of the West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals before going into private practice.

Mr. Poe began his career at The Law Offices of David L. Shuman and eventually formed the firm of Shuman, Annand and Poe in 1984. This firm, devoted to Insurance Defense Litigation, grew rapidly over the years and expanded from Charleston to Wheeling. Mr. Poe, having practiced with J. Victor Flanagan, joined Pullin, Fowler & Flanagan in 1999. During the entire course of his professional career he has devoted his work to insurance defense litigation and to the quality and cost-effective representation of insurance companies and their insureds.

Mr. Poe continues to be involved in these various activities, continues to practice the martial art of Tae Kwon Do at the S.H. Kang Tae Kwon Do Academy in South Charleston, West Virginia. He serves as legal counsel and is a member of the USTW (United States Tae Kwon Do Won). His son, Adam, is presently an undergraduate at George Washington University in Washington, D.C. His son, Sam, is presently a high school student and resides in Hilton Head, South Carolina where he enjoys fishing. Mr. Poe's daughter, Moraine, graduated from the University of California in Santa Cruz and is pursing her PhD as a Nurse Practitioner at Western University in California.

attorneys.bio:
Ryan M. Ranson serves as of-counsel for Lyne Ranson Law Offices and works under the supervision of attorney Lyne Ranson. *Mr. Ranson is not licensed to practice law in West Virginia.

Attorney Ryan Ranson heads the Ranson & Ranson law firm in Fort Lauderdale, FL. After graduating from US News "Top 25" law school, University of Florida, Levin College of Law in 2018, he immediately worked for Florida's largest law firm, "Am Law top 200" Cole Scott & Kissane, with a primary focus on commercial litigation.

In 2020, he worked for "Am Law top 100" law firm, Boies Schiller and Flexner, in Hollywood, FL. At Boies Schiller & Flexner he primarily focused on family law related matters involving high net worth individuals and their businesses. Attorney Ryan Ranson had the pleasure of representing many celebrity and notable political figures during that time.

Attorney Ryan Ranson is known for his results. His clients are quoted as saying, "Ryan is the type of attorney that goes the extra mile and does an exceptional job."

Characteristics such as integrity, determination, and being prepared, are second nature to attorney Ranson and have helped him earn a reputation of achieving optimal results for his clients. In addition, attorney Ranson's strengths of being hardworking, dedicated and knowledgeable are what he is renowned for.

In addition to his duties as an attorney, he has been able to establish and maintain a strong and effective network that has given him the ability to develop key relationships with his peers. Likewise, he is honored to serve as the 2022 American Bar Association Family Law Section Vice Chair for the Young Lawyers Association, and 2022 Vice Chair for the ABA Law Student Organization.

Further, attorney Ryan Ranson has experience litigating in federal and state court. He has represented clients located in Miami, Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach, Tampa, St. Petersburg, and Ocala, among others.

It's a well-known fact that attorney Ranson enjoys his job, specifically, helping others and their families, who would otherwise succumb to the injustices in our court system.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury -- Plaintiff Lawyers in Morgantown, WV
attorneys.bio:
West Virginia Wrongful Death Lawyer and Personal Injury Attorney In Morgantown Representing for Auto Accidents, Drilling Injuries, Mine Accidents, Morgantown Medical Malpractice, and Pipeline Explosions: Jeff Robinette, National Board Certified Trial Attorney, National Top One Percent for Personal Injury and Medical Malpractice, Super Lawyer, Multi-Million Dollar Advocates

Jeffery Robinette is a West Virginia Personal Injury Lawyer based in Morgantown who represents individuals who have been seriously injured or killed due to the irresponsible acts of an individual or company or have suffered financial losses due to property damage or professional malpractice.

Auto Accidents, Oil and Gas Rig Injury and Death, Coal Mine Injury and Death, Power Plant, and Pipeline Injuries are our firm's main focus.

As a partner in a leading West Virginia insurance defense law firm prior to founding the Robinette Legal Group, PLLC in 1999, Mr. Robinette gained valuable insight into the insurance industry claims settlement practices.

As a National Board Certified Trial Attorney who has handled hundreds of motor vehicle, injury, and construction defect claims and a leading author on insurance claims settlement issues and difficulties in West Virginia, Jeff Robinette is uniquely qualified to represent your best interest.

Prior to law school, Mr. Robinette served as an artillery, intelligence, and psychological operations officer and an accomplished paratrooper (Jump Master Qualified) in the U.S. Army's 82nd Airborne Division and is proud to have contributed to the defense of our country.

In his legal practice, Mr. Robinette offers his clients the same honor, dedication and discipline. Whether fighting an insurance claim denial or taking a personal injury claim to trial to get the best recovery for a client, he will use the strategic skills and discipline he gained in the Army to fight for your best possible result. Respect, compassion, and integrity is his guarantee to our clients, along with attention to detail and hard work.

Fighting for the Rights of the Injured

"No one expects their life will be suddenly and permanently changed as a result of a sudden, tragic event. Because wrongdoers give no advance warning of their careless behavior, even safety-minded people are not always able to avoid injury. Wherever tragedy occurs, it leaves its permanent scars on people's lives and turns their world upside down.

That's why I go to work every day: to provide you and other injury victims and their families the essential information and compassionate legal help which will enable you all to maximize your efforts to rebuild your lives." ~Jeff Robinette

Uniquely Qualified to Help You

Prior to representing injured individuals exclusively, Mr. Robinette was a partner in a major West Virginia law firm where he focused his law practice on defending serious and catastrophic injury claims, and had countless opportunities to gain inside knowledge of the operations and dangers of coal mines, power plants, and other industrial sites.

Jeff Robinette has litigated and tried numerous and varied civil cases, including serious personal injury and wrongful death cases.

He now devotes his entire law practice to representing injury victims with a focus on catastrophic injury claims. Attorney Robinette has handled hundreds of serious and catastrophic injury claims caused by motor vehicle collisions and unsafe work environments, the two leading causes of serious and catastrophic injuries in the United States.

Education and Accomplishments

Jeffery Robinette was admitted to practice law in 1991 and is licensed in all levels of state and federal trial courts in West Virginia. Mr. Robinette is also licensed in all state and federal appeals courts in West Virginia and the United States Supreme Court.

Education accomplishments include graduation from Concord College in 1983 with a degree in political science and history, and graduation from West Virginia University College of Law in 1991 where he was an editor of the West Virginia Law Review.

Legal experience also includes serving as adjunct lecturer on appellate advocacy at West Virginia University College of Law. Jeff Robinette is also a trained mediator and have completed the basic and advanced mediation training sponsored by the West Virginia State Bar.

Mr. Robinette's publishing accomplishments include serving as editor and a contributing author of the West Virginia Law Review, and he is a leading author on West Virginia injury victims' rights, having published three books for the purpose of assisting injured people and their families to understand their legal rights after a traumatic injury or tragic, unexpected death.

Memberships include of the Multi-Million Dollar Advocates Forum and Elite Lawyers of America, whose memberships are limited to lawyers who have attained multiple, multi-million dollar recoveries for personal injury victims.

Recent accomplishments include achieving the distinction of becoming a National Board Certified Trial Attorney, a designation reached by only 3% of lawyers nationwide.

Mr. Robinette is the founding member of Robinette Legal Group, PLLC, a personal injury law firm devoted to fighting for the rights of injured people throughout West Virginia. Call today to learn if we can help you.

Ms. Roush is a member of the West Virginia State Bar and is admitted to practice law in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of West Virginia and all State courts.

She provides client-focused, zealous representation in a variety of matters, including family law cases such as divorce, child custody, child support and domestic violence protective orders, as well as criminal defense, juvenile delinquency, personal injury and general civil litigation.

Raised in Shadyside, Ohio, she graduated from Shadyside High School in 2013 and earned her Bachelor of Arts from the University of Mount Union in 2016, graduating magna cum laude in just three years. She went on to earn her Juris Doctor, magna cum laude, from Case Western Reserve University in 2019. In the same year, she completed a Master of Laws in International and European Business Law from Comillas Pontifical University in Madrid, Spain, graduating at the top of her class and receiving the Concesión Premio Extraordinario distinction.

While in law school, she gained practical experience with the Cuyahoga County Prosecutor’s Office in the Child Support Unit, where she developed experience in calculating child support. She also worked with the United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Ohio under District Attorney Justin Herdman. Prior to beginning her legal career, she worked at BELCO Works, Inc., a nonprofit organization in Belmont County, Ohio, assisting individuals with special needs in securing and maintaining employment.

She is licensed to practice law in the state courts of West Virginia, Ohio and New York.

attorneys.name: Thomas E. Scarr
attorneys.practice_type: General Litigation Lawyers in Huntington, WV
attorneys.bio:
Tom Scarr is an AV-rated attorney with extensive experience in civil litigation, labor and employment law and the defense of white collar criminal matters. A veteran of multiple trials in state and federal courts, his litigation and trial experience includes handling commercial and construction disputes, personal injury litigation, premises liability, products liability and toxic tort cases, and medical, legal, accounting, and other professional liability matters. He has also handled dozens of "Mandolidis" or deliberate intent claims brought under W. Va. Code §23-4-2, and has made significant case law in the West Virginia Supreme Court of Appeals involving toxic chemical exposure claims by employees. Tom has been consistently recognized by Best Lawyers in America, Chambers USA, Benchmark Litigation and Super Lawyers in such practice areas as Commercial Litigation, Construction Law, Labor and Employment Law and ERISA.

Tom also has extensive experience in labor and employment related matters in state and federal courts and administrative bodies, including the NLRB, OSHA, EEOC, and the West Virginia Human Rights Commission. His employment practice includes preparation of employment contracts, personnel manuals and related employment policies and manuals, and providing advice concerning a variety of employment issues, including confidentiality and noncompetition agreements, FLSA, Wage & Hour, ADA, COBRA and WARN.

Tom's reputation for tenacity, thoroughness and integrity have also allowed him to develop a growing white collar criminal practice and to be sought after as a mediator in civil matters. He has the respect of both court and counsel and is an extremely effective advocate for his clients.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Weirton, WV
attorneys.bio:
As a partner at Carey & Stewart, PLLC, P. Zachary Stewart focuses his practice on personal injury and employment litigation. Mr. Stewart regularly represents clients who have been seriously injured in automobile and truck collisions, slip and fall accidents, dog bites, and as well as victims of sexual abuse. He also maintains a strong employment law practice, with particular experience in overtime and wage violations. He has helped secure six- and seven-figure recoveries in class and collective actions against employers who failed to comply with the Fair Labor Standards Act, and he represents individual employees in wage theft and retaliation claims. He is committed to helping clients level the playing field against insurance companies, large employers, and institutional defendants.

In addition to his civil litigation practice, Mr. Stewart handles criminal defense matters, including DUI defense, and provides estate planning and probate administration services for individuals and families.

A native of Weirton, West Virginia, Mr. Stewart returned home in 2013 to build a law practice defined by a client-centered approach, zealous advocacy, meticulous attention to detail, and creative legal strategies. After graduating from Weirton Madonna High School (class of 2003), he earned his Bachelor of Arts in Political Science as a University Honors Scholar from West Virginia University in 2007 and his Juris Doctor from Michigan State University College of Law in 2010. He began his career in Charleston, West Virginia, working in both state government and private practice before returning to Weirton to open his own firm. In 2023, he joined with attorney James T. Carey to form Carey & Stewart, PLLC.

Recognized for his client advocacy, Mr. Stewart has been named a Rising Star by Super Lawyers and selected to the Top 40 Under 40 Criminal Defense Lawyers by The National Trial Lawyers. He has also been recognized among the Best Attorneys for Client Satisfaction by the American Institute of Criminal Law Attorneys and holds Avvo’s highest “Superb” rating. His work has been featured in local, state, national, and international media.

Mr. Stewart is licensed in the state courts of West Virginia and Pennsylvania, the United States District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of West Virginia, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit.

He lives in Weirton, West Virginia with his wife and their two young sons.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
As a partner at Carey & Stewart, PLLC, P. Zachary Stewart focuses his practice on personal injury and employment litigation. Mr. Stewart regularly represents clients who have been seriously injured in automobile and truck collisions, slip and fall accidents, dog bites, and as well as victims of sexual abuse. He also maintains a strong employment law practice, with particular experience in overtime and wage violations. He has helped secure six- and seven-figure recoveries in class and collective actions against employers who failed to comply with the Fair Labor Standards Act, and he represents individual employees in wage theft and retaliation claims. He is committed to helping clients level the playing field against insurance companies, large employers, and institutional defendants.

In addition to his civil litigation practice, Mr. Stewart handles criminal defense matters, including DUI defense, and provides estate planning and probate administration services for individuals and families.

A native of Weirton, West Virginia, Mr. Stewart returned home in 2013 to build a law practice defined by a client-centered approach, zealous advocacy, meticulous attention to detail, and creative legal strategies. After graduating from Weirton Madonna High School (class of 2003), he earned his Bachelor of Arts in Political Science as a University Honors Scholar from West Virginia University in 2007 and his Juris Doctor from Michigan State University College of Law in 2010. He began his career in Charleston, West Virginia, working in both state government and private practice before returning to Weirton to open his own firm. In 2023, he joined with attorney James T. Carey to form Carey & Stewart, PLLC.

Recognized for his client advocacy, Mr. Stewart has been named a Rising Star by Super Lawyers and selected to the Top 40 Under 40 Criminal Defense Lawyers by The National Trial Lawyers. He has also been recognized among the Best Attorneys for Client Satisfaction by the American Institute of Criminal Law Attorneys and holds Avvo’s highest “Superb” rating. His work has been featured in local, state, national, and international media.

Mr. Stewart is licensed in the state courts of West Virginia and Pennsylvania, the United States District Courts for the Northern and Southern Districts of West Virginia, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit.

He lives in Weirton, West Virginia with his wife and their two young sons.

attorneys.name: Billie Jo Streyle
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Charleston, WV
attorneys.bio:
Billie Jo Streyle grew up on a farm where her parents instilled the value of hard work in her at a young age. Her father worked for Consol Coal and her mother was a housewife. She was the youngest of four children, and the first in her family to go to college and ultimately law school.

Billie Jo graduated summa cum laude from Waynesburg University with a Bachelor of Science degreee in computer science, a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in accounting, and a minor in business management. Her passion to help people led her to law school at Duquesne University School of Law in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania where she graduated in the year 2002 with her Juris Doctor degree.

Billie Jo is a seasoned litigator with a diverse background. She has represented clients in an array of practice areas from the inception of matters through final adjudication. In her practice, Billie Jo has engaged in jury trials and prevailed in appeals before the Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia. Apart from her accomplishments in litigation, Billie Jo also was named the first female member of a law firm, she was appointed as the Director of the West Virginia Division of Personnel by the then Governor of the State of West Virginia, and was selected as a Young Gun by West Virginia Executive Magazine.

When she is not practicing law, in her spare time, Billie Jo enjoys spending time with her daughter.

attorneys.name: Robert H. Sweeney Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: General Civil Litigation Lawyers in Huntington, WV
attorneys.bio:
Bo Sweeney has a practice based in general civil litigation, with a concentration in the defense of mesothelioma and asbestos claims, construction disputes and defending employers in deliberate intent suits brought under West Virginia Code §23-4-2. Bo serves as National Coordinating Counsel for a West Virginia based asbestos defendant, and represents numerous local and national companies in asbestos claims. A veteran of the West Virginia Asbestos Litigation since 1991, he has been trial counsel in every asbestos trial group in West Virginia since 2003, and represents manufacturers, premises owners and employers in the defense of asbestos claims throughout the state of West Virginia.

Bo also represents owners and contractors in construction litigation, and has experience in both jury trials and arbitration of construction claims and claims against sureties. He also defends employers in "Mandolidis" or deliberate intent claims brought pursuant to W. Va. Code §23-4-2. He has also handled matters involving MSHA, SMCRA, ERISA, Truth in Lending and class action litigation, and has tried over 20 cases to verdict.

sections.content:
Mr. Umina was raised in North Central, West Virginia, and is a veteran of the United States Navy. After graduating magna cum laude from the University of Illinois, he pursued his legal education.

While in law school at West Virginia University, Mr. Umina focused heavily on developing his skills as a trial attorney. During which time, he was selected for four national trial competition teams, won the prestigious Lugar Cup, and was inducted into the Order of the Barristers upon graduation.

​Mr. Umina has successfully litigated numerous cases covering a wide breadth of issues and has assisted in the recovery of millions of dollars in personal injury and wrongful death proceeds.

​In addition to his legal career, Mr. Umina has ownership interests in multiple small businesses in North Central, West Virginia. Because of this experience, he brings a unique, practical skill set to issues involving business litigation.

​Currently, he resides in the South Park area of Morgantown with his son, Kees.

attorneys.name: Montie VanNostrand
attorneys.practice_type: Social Security -- Disability Lawyers in Webster Springs, WV
attorneys.bio:
Montie VanNostrand represents injured and disabled clients of all ages in the effort to obtain monthly Social Security Disability and/or Supplemental Security Income benefits and the medical care, which accompanies these awards. She is a former chairperson of the West Virginia State Bar Committee on Social Security. She is an author of a chapter on Social Security Disability Practice in the West Virginia State Bar Handbook for West Virginia Lawyers.

Montie VanNostrand has appeared before more than a hundred different administrative law judges. She has practiced before the Offices of Hearings and Appeals of Charleston, West Virginia; Huntington, West Virginia; Morgantown, West Virginia; Pittsburgh, PA; Washington, DC; and Charlottesville, VA. She regularly files Social Security appeals in the United States District Courts of the Northern and Southern Districts of West Virginia. She is admitted to practice before the Court of Appeals of the Fourth Circuit and has practiced pro hac vice before the Court of Appeals of the Third Circuit.

Montie VanNostrand represented the appellant in Coffman v. Bowen, 829 F. 2d 514 (4th Cir. 1987). She is a sustaining member of the National Organization of Social Security Claimants, Representatives (NOSSCR) and a former member of the board of directors representing the five states of the Fourth Circuit and the District of Columbia.

Montie VanNostrand is a graduate of the West Virginia University School of Law and a member of the West Virginia State Bar. Her undergraduate degree was earned at Furman University.

Montie VanNostrand is married to the famous West Virginia potter, Brian Van Nostrand. They are the parents of Lise-Marie VanNostrand Shickert, M.A. of Louisville, Ky, and Bryson VanNostrand, architect and proprietor of Lascaux Micro Theatre, of Buckhannon, WV.

Montie VanNostrand is involved in public interest and environmental protection issues, outside of her practice of law. She is a member/supporter of the Sierra Club, World Wildlife Fund, Nature Conservancy, Union of Concerned Scientists, Natural Resources Defense Council, Green Peace, Earth Justice, Interfaith Alliance, Citizens for Global Solutions, Fair Media Project, National Committee to Protect Social Security and Medicare, A.C.T., VOTE SMART, West Virginia Citizens Action Group, Co-op America, League of Women Voters, American Civil Liberties Union, Common Cause, Friends of West Virginia Public Radio, and World Link TV.

At the local level, Montie VanNostrand and her family have been active in Put Children First, Inc. a non-profit organization dedicated to the children of Hacker Valley Grade School. She assists her community from time to time with pro bono legal projects involving country churches and cemeteries.

attorneys.name: Sarah A. Walling
attorneys.practice_type: Insurance Coverage Lawyers in Huntington, WV
attorneys.bio:
Sarah Walling joined Jenkins Fenstermaker in June 2010. Sarah focuses her practice in the areas of labor and employment litigation, insurance coverage and defense, and construction claims. She represents insurance companies and their insureds, employers, and corporations throughout West Virginia and Eastern Kentucky. Sarah has won summary judgment numerous times on complex insurance coverage issues and claims against public entities and elected officials in both state and federal courts. She has also defended cases at all stages of the litigation process and participated in mediation to obtain favorable, cost-effective results for her clients.

After graduating from the University of Texas at Austin in 2000, Sarah worked at Gracy Title Company, a Stewart Title Company affiliate located in Austin, Texas, where she assisted with the real estate closing process and issuance of title insurance for both residential and commercial properties in a rapidly expanding market. Sarah uses the knowledge and experience she gained with Gracy Title to clear title defects, defend against insurance claims, and solve legal issues that arise during eminent domain proceedings.

As a resident of Huntington, West Virginia, Sarah is active in many civic organizations. She is a Past President of the Cabell County Bar Association and the Junior League of Huntington. Sarah currently serves on the Board of Directors of the Ronald McDonald House and TEAM for West Virginia Children. She is the Vice-Chair of the Insurance Subcommittee of the Defense Trial Counsel of West Virginia and is on the Steering Committee for the Defense Research Institute's Product Liability Committee.

attorneys.name: Kristina Thomas Whiteaker
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law for Workers Lawyers in Charleston, WV
attorneys.bio:
KRISTINA THOMAS WHITEAKER is a 2003 graduate of the West Virginia University College of Law. She also received her master's degree in English Literature from Ohio University in 1999 and her undergraduate degree from Marietta College in 1995.

While in law school, she was a member of the West Virginia Law Review, was employed as a graduate research assistant for the National Environmental Services Center and clerked for the West Virginia Public Defender Services.

Kristina is admitted to practice law in West Virginia , the United States District Court for the Southern District of West Virginia, and the United States District Court for the Northern District of West Virginia. She previously practiced plaintiffs' personal injury law in Charleston with attorney Larry L. Rowe from June of 2003 to June of 2004. Kristina joined The Grubb Law Group in June of 2004.

Kristina specializes in employment discrimination law, representing victims of wrongful discharge, sexual harassment and disability discrimination. She also handles consumer protection cases involving the lemon law, fraud, unfair or deceptive business practices, warranty issues, financing issues, credit fraud and reporting abuse, and fair debt collection. Kristina's practice also concentrates on personal injury claims including car and truck accidents, motor vehicle defects and product liability.

Kristina is the mother of two sons and resides in Pinch with her husband, Ned.
